title: myCHEF vs CateringInDubai: which is better in 2026
body_html:
If you are weighing myCHEF vs CateringInDubai, the deciding question is who cooks and where. Choose myCHEF if you want a vetted chef working in your own kitchen, or catering designed around your guest count and menu. Choose CateringInDubai if you have confirmed, in writing, that its format and menu match your event better. This page sets out how to decide in 2026, using only what is publicly stated.

TL;DR
  • myCHEF is built around vetted chefs cooking in your home, plus catering designed around your event.
  • Halal-first standards and chef scoring are the myCHEF points to weigh in 2026.
  • CateringInDubai details are not verified here, so confirm menus, staffing and terms before you compare quotes.
  • Ask both for the same brief, then compare inclusions line by line, not headline totals.

The brand for this page is myCHEF, a private chef and catering service in Dubai. It offers vetted chefs for home-cooked meals, weekly meal prep, dinner parties, corporate events and large catered celebrations.

Why this matters

Two Dubai food providers can both say "catering" and mean very different things. One sends a chef to cook in your kitchen. Another prepares food elsewhere and delivers it. The gap shows up in cost structure, guest experience and how much work lands on you the day of the event.

A wrong match is expensive in a specific way. You either pay for full service you did not need, or you book a drop-off and discover nobody is plating, serving or clearing.

This comparison is written to help you decide before you request quotes. It is deliberately honest about what is not known: CateringInDubai's menus, pricing, staffing model and terms are not stated in the data behind this page, so they are treated as questions to ask, never as claims.

At a glance

Dimension myCHEF CateringInDubai
Best for Home-cooked meals, dinner parties, weekly meal prep, corporate events, large celebrations Confirm directly with the company
Core format Vetted chef in your kitchen, or catering designed around your event Confirm directly with the company
Chef vetting Chefs are vetted and scored before they cook Ask how cooks are selected and reviewed
Halal approach Halal-first standards Ask for the halal sourcing and preparation policy in writing
Menu design Designed around the client, guest count and occasion Ask whether menus are fixed or customised
Kitchen handover Kitchen left exactly as it was found Ask what cleanup is included
Pricing model Quote based on menu and guest count Ask for an itemised quote
Standout feature Chef-in-your-home service Confirm directly with the company

The rows follow the sections below, so you can jump to whichever dimension matters most.

myCHEF is the stronger fit for in-home cooking

The clearest difference is format. myCHEF places a chef in your kitchen for home-cooked meals, weekly meal prep and dinner parties. You get food cooked where you eat it, at the pace of your evening.

That matters for small, personal occasions. A dinner for six is a different job from a buffet for sixty. A chef in the room can adjust seasoning, timing and courses as the night moves.

If CateringInDubai also offers chef-in-home service, ask for the same details you would ask any provider: who the chef is, how they are chosen, and what is included in the quote. Do not assume parity from a similar category name.

Verdict: myCHEF is the safer pick for in-home dining, based on what is stated.

Vetting and standards: myCHEF states its process

myCHEF chefs are vetted and scored before they cook. That is a process you can ask about, which is more useful than a promise of quality.

It also works with halal-first standards. If halal preparation is non-negotiable for your household or guests, this is a written position you can hold the service to.

For CateringInDubai, the honest position is that its vetting and halal approach are not verified here. Ask three things:

  • How are chefs or kitchen staff selected and reviewed?
  • What is the halal sourcing and preparation policy, in writing?
  • Who is accountable if something goes wrong on the day?

Verdict: myCHEF wins on stated process. CateringInDubai is unproven here, not unfavourable.

Event scale: both can plausibly serve it, so check

myCHEF covers corporate events and large catered celebrations as well as private dining. Scale is not a differentiator on paper, and this is an honest tie until you compare live quotes.

For big events, the practical questions are the same for any provider:

  • How many guests can the team serve at once?
  • Is service staff included, or catering only?
  • What equipment is brought, and what does the venue need to supply?
  • How is the event cleared afterwards?

If your event is mostly about a delivered spread with no staff, read our guide to drop-off catering options in Dubai first. It clarifies whether you need full service at all.

Verdict: a tie until you have two quotes for the same brief.

Menu design: myCHEF designs around you

myCHEF designs menus around the client: the occasion, the guest count and dietary needs. That is a process detail worth testing. Ask any provider to send a draft menu against your brief, not a stock package.

When comparing, check whether each menu covers:

  1. Dietary requirements you have, such as halal, vegetarian, vegan or allergies.
  2. Course structure and portion planning for your guest count.
  3. What can be changed after the first draft.

Verdict: myCHEF is the better documented option for a bespoke menu. Confirm CateringInDubai's flexibility in writing.

Cleanup and the day-of experience

The brand promise at myCHEF is a kitchen left exactly as it was found. For home dinners this is often what people notice most, because a good meal in a wrecked kitchen is a poor evening.

For any provider, ask what happens after the last plate: who clears, who cleans, who removes equipment, and whether that is priced into the quote.

Verdict: myCHEF is clear on cleanup. Get the same answer from CateringInDubai before you sign.

Pricing: compare models, not headline numbers

No verified prices for either company are used on this page, so none are quoted. What you can compare is how each one prices.

  • Quote-based, designed-around-you pricing suits bespoke events. It flexes with menu and guest count, but you need a quote before you know the total.
  • Fixed package pricing is easier to compare at a glance. It can leave you paying for items you did not want, or missing items you did.

Make the comparison fair. Send both companies the same date, location, guest count and service type. Then line up what is included: chef or staff time, ingredients, equipment, service and cleanup. For context on typical ranges for chef service, see how much a private chef costs in Dubai.

Verdict: no winner on price without like-for-like quotes.

Final verdict

Choose myCHEF if:

  • You want a vetted, scored chef cooking in your own kitchen.
  • Halal-first standards are a requirement, not a preference.
  • You want a menu designed around your guests and a kitchen left as you found it.

Choose CateringInDubai if:

  • Its written quote matches your brief more closely on menu, format and inclusions.
  • It confirms staffing, halal policy and cleanup in writing to your satisfaction.
  • You have compared it against a myCHEF quote for the same date and guest count, and it wins on the details.

The quotable version: myCHEF is best for hosts who want a vetted private chef or a catering plan built around their event in Dubai in 2026.

It depends on the format you need. myCHEF is the stronger fit for a vetted chef cooking in your home. For anything else, compare written quotes for the same brief.

Does myCHEF offer halal catering in Dubai?

Yes, myCHEF works to halal-first standards. If halal preparation matters, ask for the details in your quote and confirm them before booking.

What services does myCHEF cover?

myCHEF provides vetted chefs for home-cooked meals, weekly meal prep, dinner parties, corporate events and large catered celebrations across the UAE.

How should I compare catering quotes in Dubai?

Send every provider the same date, location, guest count and service type. Then compare inclusions such as staff, equipment, service and cleanup, not just the total.

What should I ask CateringInDubai before booking?

Ask how staff are selected, what the halal policy is, whether menus can be customised, and what cleanup is included. Get every answer in writing.

Are the chefs at myCHEF vetted?

Yes. myCHEF chefs are vetted and scored before they cook for clients.

One last thing

The most useful test costs nothing. Send both companies the identical brief and see who replies with questions about your guests, kitchen and dietary needs. A provider who asks first is usually one who designs the menu around you.
